title: Generic thermodynamics of condensates with extremely small superfluid density ---Application to UTe$_2$ and hidden second phase transition---
abstract: Motivated by recent experimental findings on UTe$_2$ via NMR and specific heat experiments, we theoretically explore the thermodynamic signatures of condensates with small superfluid density and characterize their physical properties. We identify the hidden superconducting phase $A_2$ composed of spin-up Cooper pairs   at lower temperature ($T$) and field ($H$) under ambient pressure of UTe$_2$ and show that $A_2$ reappears at higher $H$ for all three principal field directions, $a$, $b$, and $c$-axis. The phase transition lines from the $A_1$ phase with spin down pairs to the $A_2$ phase in the $H$-$T$ plane are all horizontal in common, implying a universal physical origin due to the originating from the magnetic-energy gain of the spin-up pairing state with increasing magnetic field. This multiple-phase diagram is extended to these under pressure ($P$), resulting in a simple picture based on non-unitary spin-triplet pairing symmetry $^3B_{3u}$, which enables us to consistently capture the evolution of the superconducting phases throughout the entire $H$-$T$-$P$ phase space.
summary: This work theoretically investigates the thermodynamics of superconductors with very low superfluid density, using UTe2 as a primary example. The authors predict the existence of a hidden second superconducting phase ($A_2$) and unify the phase diagram using a non-unitary spin-triplet pairing symmetry. By analyzing key observables like $1/T_1$ and $C(T)$, the paper provides a comprehensive theoretical picture for complex, multi-phase superconducting behavior.
main_problem: The paper theoretically explores the thermodynamic signatures of superconducting condensates exhibiting extremely small superfluid density, motivated by experimental findings in UTe2.
main_result: It identifies a hidden second superconducting phase ($A_2$) in UTe2, suggesting a universal origin for the phase transition lines based on non-unitary spin-triplet pairing symmetry ($^3B_{3u}$).
method: The analysis uses theoretical derivations for generic thermodynamics of low-$ho_s$ condensates, calculating observables like the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate ($1/T_1$) and specific heat ($C(T)$).
model_or_system: The system is the heavy Fermion superconductor UTe2. The theoretical framework involves modeling superconductivity using a non-unitary spin-triplet pairing symmetry, allowing for the description of multiple superconducting phases across the H-T-P phase space.
key_observables: Superfluid density ($ho_s$), phase stiffness, nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate ($1/T_1$), specific heat jump ($\Delta C$), and the existence of multiple superconducting phases ($A_1, A_2$).
important_parameters: Small superfluid density ($ho_s$), the gap ratio ($\alpha = \Delta_0/k_B T_c$), and external parameters like magnetic field ($H$) and pressure ($P$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the limit of extremely small superfluid density, which suppresses characteristic superconducting signatures like the Hebel-Slichter peak.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams in the H-T plane for different field directions, showing the coexistence of $A_1$ and $A_2$ phases, and plot the temperature dependence of $1/T_1$ and $C(T)$ for varying $\alpha$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from analyzing the general thermodynamic signatures of low-$ho_s$ condensates, applies these concepts to the specific case of UTe2, and develops a unified phase diagram incorporating multiple superconducting phases ($A_1$ and $A_2$) across the H-T-P space.
why_interesting: The theoretical modeling of unconventional superconductivity, particularly the incorporation of spin-triplet pairing and the analysis of suppressed thermodynamic signatures, connects directly to advanced topics in strongly correlated electron physics relevant to AMO/quantum materials research.
